title: Measurement: Packaging and Optimisation
summary: Surface area and volume of packaging, comparing package designs, packing arrangements, cost of materials, and using conversions and formulas in practical problems.

notes.text: Businesses choose packaging that holds the product, uses little material (lower cost and less waste), stacks and packs efficiently into boxes and trucks, and looks attractive.

notes.title: Worked example 1: comparing two designs
notes.problem: A juice company needs a 1 ℓ (1 000 cm³) container. Design A: a box 10 cm × 10 cm × 10 cm. Design B: a cylinder with radius 5,5 cm and height 10,5 cm. Which uses less material? Use $\pi = 3{,}142$.
steps: A: volume 1 000 cm³; surface area = 6 × 100 = 600 cm²
B holds about the same volume with less material.
notes.answer: The cylinder uses about 47 cm² less material

notes.label: But…
notes.text: Cylinders waste space when packed into rectangular boxes. In a square arrangement, circles cover only about 79% of the floor of the box, so boxes may need to be bigger.

notes.title: Worked example 2
notes.problem: Cans with diameter 7 cm and height 12 cm are packed upright in a box 42 cm × 28 cm × 24 cm. How many cans fit?

notes.title: Worked example 3
notes.problem: Cardboard costs R0,04 per 100 cm². A company makes 25 000 boxes of 600 cm² each. What is the cost of cardboard?

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: In ML exams, formulas and conversions are usually given. Write the formula, substitute carefully (with units), and check whether the question asks for cm², m², cm³ or litres.

questions.prompt: Find the volume of a box 25 cm × 20 cm × 8 cm, in litres.
Find the surface area of a closed box 10 cm × 6 cm × 4 cm.
A tin has radius 4 cm and height 11 cm. Calculate its volume in cm³ using $\pi = 3{,}142$, to one decimal place.
Boxes 12 cm × 8 cm × 5 cm are packed into a carton 48 cm × 32 cm × 30 cm (same orientation). How many fit?
Cylinders packed in a rectangular box leave empty space between them.
A label wraps around a can of radius 3,5 cm and height 10 cm, with a 1 cm overlap. Calculate the length and area of the label. Use $\pi = 3{,}142$.
questions.memo:
✓ Circumference 2 × 3,142 × 3,5 = 21,99 cm (1)
✓ Length with overlap 22,99 cm (1)
✓ Area ≈ 229,9 cm² (1)

questions.prompt: Plastic for bottles costs R1,20 per 1 000 cm². Each bottle needs 450 cm². What does the plastic cost for 10 000 bottles?
Give TWO reasons why a company might choose a rectangular box rather than a cylinder for cereal.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): packs without wasted space; stacks easily on shelves; large flat surfaces for advertising; easy to make from cardboard

questions.prompt: A container holds 2 500 cm³. How many litres is this?
